reply: 20 April 2026 falls in the high season. The Easter 2026 peak runs from 21 March 2026 to 20 April 2026, so the high season baggage fee applies. Fees also vary by bag weight and by whether you pay online, through the Call Centre or at the airport. For example, a high season max. 10 kg bag booked on WIZZAIR.COM or through the Call Centre costs €9.00 – €115.00 per flight, per passenger and per bag. The excerpts do not say whether 20 April counts as a peak day for every purpose, so check with Wizz Air if you need certainty.

question: Can I put a power bank and spare lithium batteries in my checked suitcase if I switch them off and wrap them separately?
reference: No. Power banks must not be in checked baggage, and spare lithium batteries must be carried in cabin baggage only, individually protected from short circuits.
reply: No. Power banks must not be put in checked baggage and must be carried where you can continuously monitor them during the flight. Spare batteries are also forbidden in checked baggage, even if they are individually protected, and must be carried in cabin baggage only. Switching them off or wrapping them does not change this.

question: My small backpack can be 45 x 35 x 20 cm for free, right? I don't have to pay for priority if it fits under the seat?
reference: No. The free carry-on is 40 x 30 x 20 cm, so 45 x 35 x 20 cm is too big and will be charged (cabin baggage fee at the airport €55.00 – €65.00). Fitting under the seat does not matter; a bag up to 55 x 40 x 23 cm needs WIZZ Priority.
reply: No. The free carry-on bag must be no larger than 40 x 30 x 20 cm and 10 kg, and it must fit under the seat in front of you. A 45 x 35 x 20 cm backpack is larger than that, so it would not be free, and exceeding the dimensions results in extra fees. You do not need WIZZ Priority for the free carry-on bag, since every passenger is entitled to one. Priority is only needed for the larger trolley bag allowance of 55 x 40 x 23 cm.

question: We're travelling with a 6-month-old baby and have a stroller plus a small musical instrument. Can we bring both without an additional baggage fee?
reference: The foldable stroller is free for the infant, but a musical instrument is special baggage for an additional fee (on board only with WIZZ Priority).
reply: The stroller can be taken free of charge: for an infant, a foldable baby pushchair or pram may be brought on board. It can be taken up to the aircraft door or steps, then stowed in the hold and tagged at check-in, the baggage drop-off desk or the boarding gate. Electric or motorized strollers are not allowed. The musical instrument is free on board only if you have WIZZ Priority added to your booking. It must be in a case up to 80 x 40 x 23 cm and 10 kg, it takes the place of a trolley bag, and it goes in the overhead compartment. Without WIZZ Priority, special baggage is charged an additional fee, and the sources do not give that fee or the rules for carrying an instrument without Priority.

question: Can I take a power bank on the plane?
reference: Power banks must be in cabin baggage where you can monitor them, never in checked baggage; max. 1 power bank per person, over 100 Wh is forbidden, and it may not be used during the flight.
reply: Yes, but only in cabin baggage, never in checked baggage. Power banks must not be used during any phase of the flight and must be kept where you can continuously monitor them, on your person. Power banks over 100 Wh are forbidden. Those rated 100 to 160 Wh need Wizz Air's approval. You may carry a maximum of 1 power bank, within a limit of 20 spare batteries. A power bank cannot be charged or used to charge another device during the flight, and it cannot go in the overhead compartments; it must be placed under the seat in front or in the seat back pocket.
